channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: The 9 Lives Of A Frontline Ukrainian Aid Worker
item.description: Yevhen Tkachov, an aid worker with the NGO Proliska, has spent years helping Ukrainians evacuate from war-torn towns and villages. He's had more narrow escapes from enemy fire than he can count and has caught some harrowing scenes on camera as drones and missiles hit nearby.

item.title: Hague War Crimes Trial Casts Shadow Over Kosovo's 18th Birthday Celebrations
item.description: The anniversary of Kosovo's declaration of independence is being overshadowed by the trial of the man who proclaimed it, former President Hashim Thaci, and in particular by the prosecution's request for a 45-year prison sentence.

item.title: Witkoff Cites 'Meaningful Progress' On First Day Of US-Brokered Talks Between Russia, Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian and Russian negotiators were set to meet for the latest round of US-brokered peace talks following another round of Russian overnight strikes on targets across Ukraine with hundreds of drones and missiles.

item.title: Following Iran Nuclear Talks, China's Support For Tehran Returns To The Spotlight
item.description: Targeting Iran’s oil sales to China could test the limits of Beijing’s backing as Washington seeks leverage in renewed nuclear negotiations.

item.title: No Agreement Reached In Latest Round Of US-Iran Talks In Geneva
item.description: A second round of indirect talks between Iran and the United States over Tehran's nuclear program concluded on February 17, according to Iran's state broadcaster.

item.title: Wider Europe Briefing: Ukraine's 2027 EU Dream And What Brussels Wants From Moscow
item.description: Could Ukraine really join the EU next year?

item.title: EU Pushes Ukraine On Repair Of Druzhba Pipeline Carrying Russian Oil To Hungary, Slovakia
item.description: A European Commission spokeswoman on February 17 confirmed that Brussels was in touch with Ukraine regarding the Druzhba pipeline that has been damaged since late January, preventing Russian oil from flowing to Hungary and Slovakia.

item.title: Teen Kickbox Champ Killed in War Honored On Banned Olympic Helmet
item.description: Karina Bakhur, a 17-year-old kickboxing champion killed by a Russian missile in Ukraine, is honored on Ukrainian Olympian Vladyslav Heraskevych’s helmet. He was banned from competing in skeleton for the tribute. Bakhur's father says he is proud that his daughter's memory lives on.

item.title: State Department: No 'Gentleman's Agreement' Between US, Russia On Expired Nuclear Treaty
item.description: A senior US State Department official has flatly rejected suggestions that Washington and Moscow are informally continuing to observe the limits of the now-expired, nuclear-weapon-limiting New START treaty, saying there is no “gentlemen’s agreement” in place.

item.title: Archaeologists Launch 'Virtual Museum' To Ukraine's Ancient Heritage
item.description: An online museum aims to make Ukraine’s heritage accessible to the public while many of the featured treasures remain impossible to view in person.
